situation: UP won by an innings and 267 runs
notes: Madhav Kaushik (150) and Rinku Singh (112) added a 200-plus stand from 3 down on day one | Bihar were bowled out twice inside 4 sessions | Zeeshan Ansari 4-40 finished it after the follow-on
result: UP won by an innings and 267 runs
endSummary: Uttar Pradesh opened their season with the most lopsided result of the round, beating Bihar by an innings and 267 runs in Rajgir. Madhav Kaushik's 150 and a Rinku Singh hundred built 540, and Bihar never got within 400 — bowled out for 141 and 132, with Kartik Yadav and Zeeshan Ansari taking four apiece.

situation: Baroda won by an innings and 135 runs
notes: Goa lost their last six follow-on wickets for 20 on the final day | Baroda's top six all got starts; Atit Sheth fell one short of a hundred (99) | Mahesh Pithiya 5-58 and Bhargav Bhatt 4-51 shared nine of ten in the first innings
result: Baroda won by an innings and 135 runs
endSummary: Baroda converted a 273-run first-innings lead into an innings-and-135-run win in Panaji, rolling Goa over for 138 in the follow-on on the final day. A deep batting card, led by Atit Sheth's 99 and Mitesh Patel's 81, set up 472 for 8, and Mahesh Pithiya's 5 for 58 and Bhargav Bhatt's 4 for 51 did the rest.

notes: Puducherry bowled out for 130 in 41.1 overs chasing 291 | Harsh Dubey 4-29 and Parth Rekhade 3-43 shared seven | Akshay Wadkar's 198 (player of the match) was the round's top score | Yash Rathod added 134
endSummary: Vidarbha opened with a 160-run win in Nagpur, bowling Puducherry out for 130 in just 41.1 overs on the final day. Akshay Wadkar's 198, the highest score of the round, and Yash Rathod's 134 built 428, and after a quick 175 for 3 declaration Harsh Dubey's 4 for 29 and Parth Rekhade's 3 for 43 finished it with time to spare.

situation: Match drawn; J&K held on at 88/7, MP took first-innings lead
notes: J&K survived at 88/7 after bad light ate into the final day | Avesh Khan 3-16 and Aryan Pandey 3-29 had them 61/6 | Auqib Nabi's 30 off 32 and Kanhaiya Wadhawan's 27 saw them through | MP banked first-innings points after bowling the champions out for 120
result: Match drawn — Madhya Pradesh took first-innings lead
endSummary: Champions Jammu & Kashmir escaped with a draw in Srinagar, finishing 88 for 7 chasing 326 after bad light cut into Madhya Pradesh's push. Avesh Khan (3 for 16) and Aryan Pandey (3 for 29) had them 61 for 6, but Auqib Nabi's 30 off 32 and Kanhaiya Wadhawan's return from retired hurt held MP to first-innings points, earned when J&K were bowled out for 120.

situation: Match drawn; Punjab took first-innings lead
notes: Assam finished 157/6, 52 ahead, as the game petered out | Punjab's 478/6d earned a 105-run lead | Vihaan Malhotra 103 on first-class debut | Umesh Yadav 5-70 on Punjab debut; Sibsankar Roy 143* for Assam
result: Match drawn — Punjab took first-innings lead
endSummary: Punjab took first-innings points in New Chandigarh, declaring at 478 for 6 for a 105-run lead after Vihaan Malhotra's debut hundred. Umesh Yadav's 5 for 70 on his Punjab debut had kept Assam to 373 despite Sibsankar Roy's unbeaten 143, and Assam batted out the last day at 157 for 6.

situation: Match drawn; Saurashtra took first-innings lead
notes: Saurashtra batted out the last day at 229/1, 309 ahead | Ravindra Jadeja's 102 and 3-40 made it a useful Test warm-up | Prerak Mankad 129 anchored the 392 | 80-run first-innings lead decided the points
result: Match drawn — Saurashtra took first-innings lead
endSummary: Saurashtra banked first-innings points against Chhattisgarh in Rajkot and batted out the last day at 229 for 1. The headline was Ravindra Jadeja's all-round return, 102 and 3 for 40, alongside Prerak Mankad's 129 that built an 80-run lead.

situation: Match drawn; Andhra took first-innings lead
notes: Andhra closed at 104/4, 90 short of 194 | Karun Nair's 145* turned a 144-run deficit into a declaration | Seeram Rahul 119 earned Andhra the lead | KL Rahul made 4 and 1 before the NZ tour
result: Match drawn — Andhra took first-innings lead
endSummary: Andhra held on for a draw and first-innings points in Vijayawada, closing at 104 for 4 after Karnataka set 194. Karun Nair's unbeaten 145 had turned a 144-run deficit into a sporting declaration, but Seeram Rahul's 119 in Andhra's 418 had already decided the points; KL Rahul managed 4 and 1.

situation: Hyderabad won by an innings and 40 runs
notes: Tripura offspinner Sandip Sarkar took 8-96 in only his fourth first-class game — in a losing cause | Tanay Thyagarajan: 9 wickets in the match, 6-52 in the second | Siraj went wicketless in the first innings
result: Hyderabad won by an innings and 40 runs
endSummary: Hyderabad beat Tripura by an innings and 40 runs, but the performance of the match came from the losing side: Tripura offspinner Sandip Sarkar took 8 for 96 in just his fourth first-class game. Left-arm spinner Tanay Thyagarajan's nine-wicket match, including 6 for 52 second time around, decided it.

notes: Siddharth Desai 5-36 bowled Odisha out for 161 on the final day | Gujarat knocked off 47 without loss | Vedant Trivedi 108 and Aarya Desai 94 built a 115-run first-innings lead | Gourav Choudhury's career-best 137 in vain
endSummary: Gujarat turned a 115-run first-innings lead into a 10-wicket win in Ahmedabad, the round's only outright result decided on the last day in Group C. Vedant Trivedi's 108 and Aarya Desai's 94 overhauled Gourav Choudhury's career-best 137, then Siddharth Desai's 5 for 36 bowled Odisha out for 161 and left a target of just 47.

notes: Bengal chased 89 in 15.3 overs after Delhi's last pair fell | Ayush Badoni 85 and 5-43 almost saved Delhi single-handed | Abishek Porel 149 (player of the match) and Sudip Gharami 133 rebuilt from 132/6 | Mohammed Shami 4-30 in the first innings
endSummary: Bengal beat Delhi by nine wickets in Kalyani, chasing 89 in 15.3 overs after Delhi's follow-on resistance ended at 277. Abishek Porel's 149 and Sudip Gharami's 133 rescued Bengal from 132 for 6 to 429, and Mohammed Shami's 4 for 30 forced the follow-on. Ayush Badoni's 5 for 43 and 85 made him the best player on the losing side.

situation: Match drawn; Jharkhand took the first-innings lead
notes: Kerala finished 62/2 in the follow-on, still 130 behind | Jharkhand's 587 had three hundreds: Aditya Singh 147, Shikhar Mohan 143, Virat Singh 108 | Utkarsh Singh (71 & 5-84) was player of the match | Abhishek P Nair 126 the lone first-innings resistance
result: Match drawn — Jharkhand took first-innings lead
endSummary: Jharkhand banked first-innings points in Jamshedpur on the back of a 587 that carried three hundreds, Aditya Singh's 147 and Shikhar Mohan's 143 leading the way. Utkarsh Singh's 71 and five wickets made him player of the match, and Kerala, forced to follow on despite Abhishek P Nair's 126, batted out the last day at 62 for 2.

notes: Services lost their last four for 9 after tea, all out for 120 | Vicky Ostwal 5-50 in 28 overs; Siddhesh Veer 3-27 | Arjun Sharma's nine-wicket match went in vain | Ankit Bawne 118 and Hitesh Walunj (7 wkts in match) set it up
endSummary: Maharashtra won by 127 runs at Palam, bowling Services out for 120 after they had reached tea at 111 for 6 chasing 248. Left-arm spinner Vicky Ostwal took 5 for 50 in 28 overs, backing up Ankit Bawne's first-innings 118 and Hitesh Walunj's 5 for 51. Services seamer Arjun Sharma's nine wickets in the match went unrewarded.

situation: Mumbai won by an innings and 155 runs
notes: Tushar Deshpande 5-17 with a hat-trick (five in 16 balls) | Jaiswal 0, Sarfaraz 1 — the lower order made the runs | Kotian 58 & 3-30
result: Mumbai won by an innings and 155 runs
endSummary: Mumbai crushed Chandigarh by an innings and 155 runs at the Wankhede despite Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sarfaraz Khan managing one run between them. Siddhesh Lad (86) and the lower order built 429, then Tushar Deshpande ripped through Chandigarh with 5 for 17, including a hat-trick, to bowl them out for 78.

situation: Match drawn; Rajasthan took first-innings lead
notes: Tamil Nadu 73/0 when the game was called off — no result chase | Kukna Ajay Singh (5-51) was player of the match | Karan Lamba 113 and Rohan Rajbhar 95 built 363 | N Jagadeesan 42* in the second innings
result: Match drawn — Rajasthan took first-innings lead
endSummary: Rajasthan took first-innings points in Jaipur in a game that ended with Tamil Nadu 73 for 0, 209 short of a target of 282. Karan Lamba's 113 built 363, and player of the match Kukna Ajay Singh's 5 for 51 earned an 89-run lead.

notes: Chased 71 for the loss of only three on the final morning | HP collapsed for 113 second time around after a 43-run first-innings deficit | Akash Vasisht 113* carried HP's first innings; Anshul Kamboj took four
endSummary: Haryana closed out a 7-wicket win in Rohtak, knocking off a target of 71 on the final morning. The game turned on Himachal's second-innings collapse to 113, with Parth Vats taking 3 for 22, after Anshul Kamboj's 4 for 56 had already wiped out the value of Akash Vasisht's unbeaten 113. It's the only Elite result so far not won by an innings.

situation: Match drawn; Uttarakhand took first-innings lead
notes: Railways batted 86 overs for 272/4 to save it | Vivek Singh followed his 112 with 58; Suraj Ahuja 53 | Saurabh Rawat 107 (player of the match) built a 192-run lead | Devendra Bora 5-49 on day one
result: Match drawn — Uttarakhand took first-innings lead
endSummary: Uttarakhand took first-innings points at the Brabourne, but Railways comfortably saved the game at 272 for 4. Saurabh Rawat's 107, which made him player of the match, built a 192-run lead after Devendra Bora's 5 for 49; Vivek Singh added 58 to his first-innings 112 to see Railways home.

situation: Match drawn; Meghalaya took first-innings lead
notes: Sikkim finished 291/7, 141 ahead | Jaskirat Singh 127 earned Meghalaya a 150-run lead | Ram Gurung 5-32 bowled Sikkim out on day one | Parth Palawat 66 led the rearguard
result: Match drawn — Meghalaya took first-innings lead
endSummary: Meghalaya took first-innings points in Rangpo, with Ram Gurung's 5 for 32 and Jaskirat Singh's 127 building a 150-run lead. Sikkim batted out the final day at 291 for 7, led by Parth Palawat's 66.

notes: Manipur recovered from 84/5 to chase 228 | Pheiroijam Jotin Singh 105 (player of the match) and Johnson Singh 51 | Kishan Singha 10 wkts in match (6-52 & 4-88) | Khiangte Vanrotlinga 3-42 for Mizoram
endSummary: Manipur pulled off the chase of the round in Nadiad, getting to 228 for 7 from 84 for 5 to win by three wickets. Pheiroijam Jotin Singh's 105 and Johnson Singh's 51 did the batting, after Kishan Singha's 10-wicket match (6 for 52 and 4 for 88) kept Manipur in it.

notes: No ball bowled in Ahmedabad | Forfeit stems from a factional dispute in the Arunachal Cricket Association that has reached the courts | Arunachal also missed U-19 and U-23 fixtures this week
result: Nagaland awarded the match (Arunachal Pradesh forfeit)
endSummary: Nagaland start their Plate campaign with a result they never had to play for: Arunachal Pradesh forfeited the opener in Ahmedabad. Arunachal's association is split between two rival factions in a court dispute, and the fallout has already cost them fixtures at U-19 and U-23 level this week.
